effort: Compress into a lateral plant and drive from a shuffle into a running exit.
brief: E2 links lateral braking to forward acceleration. Short elastic foot contacts, an open first step, two-foot lateral acceptance, one rebound return and a grounded lateral ball projection each isolate a different contributor. The strength focus is frontal-plane acceptance supported by hip and ankle force.
marker: On each shuffle-to-sprint attempt, note whether the athlete slows the lateral approach before opening the hips and sends the first two running steps down the exit, without an upright hop.
readiness: Confirm stable lateral landings and the ability to open the hips without twisting on a fixed knee. Use a low-amplitude rebound only when the first bound lands under control; otherwise shorten both bounds without adding a new drill.
space: E2 requires a measured 8 m × 4 m clear bay: 1 m lateral entry, 2 m forward exit and 3 m final stop, with side/escape margins. Its transverse width is a requirement, not confirmed by the lane inventory. Other travel and the ball projection can be oriented along one 10 m lane.

drills.name: Lateral Line Pogo
drills.execution: Both feet take off and land together, alternating across a line by only a few centimetres.
drills.job: Brief ankle-driven force reversals before larger lateral plants; keep the support dose very small.
drills.layout: Use the middle of a cleared lane; no obstacle height. Finish the sixth landing and reset.
drills.difference: Repeated bilateral ankle rebounds; unlike Class 1's single-flight opposite-leg bound and grounded shuffles.
drills.regress: Reduce excursion and cadence if contacts become loud or posture folds.
drills.exposure: 6 low-amplitude bilateral landings; final landing included.

drills.name: Shuffle-to-Sprint Transition
drills.execution: Shuffle 1 m, brake before the corner, open the hips and accelerate 2 m forward; stop over the next 3 m.
drills.job: Main lateral-to-forward force transfer; change locomotion and direction without jumping upright.
drills.layout: Set a 1 m lateral approach perpendicular to a 2 m exit plus 3 m stop. Mirror one side at a time within the stated bay.
drills.difference: Moving lateral entry into an orthogonal running exit, unlike the stationary crossover start or same-facing reversal in Class 1.
drills.regress: Slow the shuffle if feet cross early or the turn becomes a locked-foot pivot.
drills.exposure: 1 direction change, 1 turn-braking phase and 1 terminal stop; no prescribed jump.

drills.name: Lateral Open-Step to Sprint
drills.execution: From a side-facing athletic stance, the near leg opens toward the exit first; accelerate 2 m, stop over 3 m. No crossover first step.
drills.job: Isolate a direct hip-opening exit when crossing the legs would delay the push.
drills.layout: Start near metre 2 and drive toward 4, stopping by 7; mirror from 8 toward 6, stopping by 3.
drills.difference: Near-leg open step replaces Class 1's far-leg crossover; this is a different first contact sequence, not a faster copy.
drills.regress: Use a smaller opening step and slower first attempt if the planted knee twists.
drills.exposure: One stationary initiation and terminal stop; no incoming-momentum cut.

drills.name: Lateral Hop to Stick — bilateral
drills.execution: Two-foot lateral takeoff and landing, comfortable travel no more than 0.5 m; hold 2 s.
drills.job: Accept lateral force through a shared base while keeping pelvis and trunk organized.
drills.layout: Centre of lane, facing across it so lateral travel follows its length; clear 2 m beyond either landing.
drills.difference: Bilateral takeoff and landing with a terminal hold, unlike single-leg bounds or continuous line rebounds.
drills.regress: Shorten travel if either foot lands markedly earlier or the knees collapse inward.

drills.name: Skater Bound Continuous — one out-and-back pair
drills.execution: Bound laterally onto the opposite leg, reverse immediately for one return bound, then hold 2 s. Each flight stays within 0.5 m.
drills.job: Practice absorption turning into another lateral push rather than ending every landing in stillness.
drills.layout: One cleared lane, centre near 5 m; 2 flights only, no continuing skater circuit.
drills.difference: Two linked opposite-leg flights with one active rebound; Class 1's bound ends in a static hold.
drills.regress: Reduce both distances; stop if the first landing cannot support the return without a recovery step.
drills.exposure: 2 unilateral landings, one on each leg, per pair; flight reversal is not logged as a running cut.

drills.name: Grounded Lateral Scoop Slam
drills.execution: Use a light slam ball; shift from the outside hip and drive it low and diagonally down into the floor 1 m to the side. Feet stay grounded.
drills.job: Express lateral leg-to-trunk force against an external load without adding landing contacts.
drills.layout: Orient the throw along the lane, release into an empty 1 m target area and clear all bounce/retrieval space. Use an appropriate low-bounce ball. If clearance/floor use is unsuitable, use instead Stationary Lateral Push-Start Shuffle: 1 × 2 each direction, push from stillness into 2 m shuffle and stop over 2 m; rest 60 s between attempts. This proposed replacement starts square with no crossover or hip-opening run.
drills.difference: Grounded externally resisted lateral projection; no earlier ballistic throw slot exists.
drills.regress: Use a lighter ball and shorter release if arm effort replaces the lateral hip drive.
drills.exposure: 1 ball release, no intended athlete flight. Replacement removes 4 throws and adds 4 shuffle attempts, 8 m travel plus up to 8 m stopping, and 4 terminal braking episodes; allow up to 2 extra minutes.

light.job: Control the hip and knee during a lateral plant before a running exit.
Keep the outside foot edge controlled when the lateral approach is braked.

strength.job: Main frontal-plane acceptance and push-back strength for the shuffle plant.
Retain hip-hinge force for driving the first running exit.
A small lead-leg knee/hip dose supports the new forward step after lateral braking.
Heel-dig knee-flexor support complements the moving hinge without another heavy knee-dominant set.
Adductor support limits unwanted sideways pelvic drop in the lateral plant.
Bent-knee ankle force supports lateral compression and the first push.

previous_review: Class 1 prescribed 18 locomotor attempts, four unilateral landings and 13 primary bouts; actual response is unknown. Its six drill identities were reserved against reuse.
progression: New lateral transitions replace the earlier reversals; they do not imply a faster entry was earned. Running attempts drop while modest bilateral elastic/landing work is introduced; these loads are tracked separately.
strength_progression: Retain the same RIR and technique on lateral lunge, RDL, split squat, bridge, Copenhagen and soleus. Reduce split squat to one round per side because the new rebound work adds lateral acceptance. No load increase is prescribed without actual feedback.
audit: Reduced the main shuffle entry to 1 m so stopping and the 90-degree exit can be planned in a compact bay. Kept only one rebound pair each way and one lateral-lunge round. Grounded ball work replaces another jump exposure; no throwing wall is assumed.
next: Next class: introduce a diagonal exit at controlled entry speed; first review this class's side-specific control, actual load and any new feedback.

light_entries.name: Mini-Band Lateral Walk
light_entries.execution: Very light loop above knees; small quiet steps, toes forward and knees aligned. Both directions are one set round.
light_entries.regress: Use a lighter band/smaller step if pelvis sways or the task burns.
light_entries.job: Control the hip and knee during a lateral plant before a running exit.

light_entries.name: Seated Band Ankle Eversion — self-anchored (proposed)
light_entries.execution: Sit securely, use the other foot to hold a light loop; turn the working forefoot slightly outward against tension, 2 s return, keep knee still.
light_entries.regress: Use less tension/range for toe gripping or whole-leg rotation.
light_entries.source: Proposed exact setup; no verified identifier
light_entries.alternative: Use instead of the band, gentle hand resistance at the outer forefoot with the same easy reps if a loop cannot be secured.
light_entries.job: Keep the outside foot edge controlled when the lateral approach is braked.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Main frontal-plane acceptance and push-back strength for the shuffle plant.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Retain hip-hinge force for driving the first running exit.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: A small lead-leg knee/hip dose supports the new forward step after lateral braking.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Heel-dig knee-flexor support complements the moving hinge without another heavy knee-dominant set.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Adductor support limits unwanted sideways pelvic drop in the lateral plant.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Bent-knee ankle force supports lateral compression and the first push.
